newsitem.title: UK: GrandMet unit says considers U.S. TV alcohol ads.
newsitem.headline: GrandMet unit says considers U.S. TV alcohol ads.

text.p: A unit of Grand Metropolitan Plc, whose brands include Smirnoff and Jack Daniels, said Friday the British food and drinks group was considering advertising alcohol on television in the United States.
Last week the head of the U.S. Federal Communications Commission criticised Seagram Co. Ltd and certain television stations in the United States for airing commercials for hard liquor.
In June, Seagram ended the liquor industry's decades-old tradition in the United States of not advertising on TV.
The decision fuelled controversy in the alcohol industry and unleashed criticism from President Clinton and members of Congress.
Recent press reports said GrandMet was looking at the possibility of advertising its Bailey's Irish Cream Liqueur on American television.

"We're looking at it as a possibility. It's at a very early stage and we are a long way from making a decision, but we certainly hope to get the opportunity," a spokesman for R&A Bailey said, when asked about the press reports.
R&A Bailey makes Bailey's Irish Cream and is part of IDV, which is owned by GrandMet.
The spokesman said the subject was a sensitive issue and that no advertisements had been created for any such future ad campaign.
Representative Joe Kennedy, D.-Mass., criticised Seagram last week for its decision to advertise on television and appealed to the FCC to investigate the impact of the advertising on children.

A Seagram spokeswoman said the company had been considering entering broadcast advertising for some time. She said the "media landscape" had changed since 1948, when the alcohol industry voluntarily banned television advertising, and Seagram was now able to target its ads to the adult market.
